lines.text: Ex Heliodori commentario in Paulum Alexandrinum 1.
lines.en: From Heliodorus' commentary on Paulus Alexandrinus 1.

lines.text: (F. 11v). Ἰστέον τοίνυν ὅτι περὶ τῶν τοιούτων κλήρων Ἑρμῇ τῷ
lines.en: (Fol. 11v). It must be known, then, that concerning such lots it has been written by Hermes

lines.text: Τρισμεγίστῳ γέγραπται ἐν βίβλῳ τῇ καλουμένῃ Παναρέτῳ 2, ἔνθα
lines.en: Trismegistus in the book called Panaretos 2, where

lines.text: καὶ τὰ ἀποτελέσματα τούτων παραδίδωσι, δι’ ὧν καὶ μόνων ἂν δύναιτό
lines.en: he also hands down their outcomes, through which alone

lines.text: τις ἐφ’ ἑκάστου πράγματος προλέγειν τὰ συμβησόμενα χωρὶς ἑτέρας
lines.en: one would be able to foretell the things that will happen concerning each matter without any other

lines.text: 5 τινὸς ἐπισκέψεως· οὗτος οὖν ὁ θεῖος ἀνὴρ ἑπτὰ ἔφη εἶναι κλήρους κατὰ
lines.en: 5 examination; this divine man, then, said that there are seven lots according to

lines.text: τὸν ἀριθμὸν τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀστέρων, καὶ ὠνόμασε τὸν μὲν κλῆρον τοῦ Ἡλίου
lines.en: the number of the seven stars, and he named the lot of the Sun

lines.text: Ἀγαθὸν Δαίμονα, τὸν δὲ κλῆρον τῆς Σελήνης Ἀγαθὴν Τύχην, τὸν δὲ
lines.en: Good Daimon, and the lot of the Moon Good Fortune, and the

lines.text: κλῆρον τοῦ Διὸς Νίκην, τὸν δὲ τοῦ Ἑρμοῦ (f. 12) Ἀνάγκην, τὸν δὲ τῆς
lines.en: lot of Zeus Victory, and that of Hermes (fol. 12) Necessity, and that of

lines.text: Ἀφροδίτης Ἔρωτα, τὸν δὲ τοῦ Ἄρεως Τόλμην, τὸν δὲ τοῦ Κρόνου
lines.en: Aphrodite Eros, and that of Ares Daring, and that of Kronos

lines.text: 10 Νέμεσιν· οὐ μάτην δὲ ταῦτα ἐθέσπισεν, ἀλλ’ ἐπειδὴ οἷα τις τύχη τοῦ
lines.en: 10 Nemesis; and he did not ordain these things in vain, but since the Moon is like a certain fortune of the

lines.text: παντός ἐστιν ἡ Σελήνη, τούτου χάριν τὸν κλῆρον αὐτῆς Ἀγαθὴν Τύχην
lines.en: universe, for this reason he named her lot Good Fortune,

lines.text: ὠνόμασεν, ἐπειδὴ δὲ καὶ ὁ Ἥλιος ἔφορός ἐστι τοῦ παντός, τούτου
lines.en: and since the Sun is also the overseer of the universe, for this

lines.text: χάριν τὸν κλῆρον αὐτοῦ Ἀγαθὸν Δαίμονα ἐκάλεσεν· ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ
lines.en: reason he called his lot Good Daimon; and similarly also

lines.text: τὸν τοῦ Διὸς Νίκην, ἐπειδὴ ὁ Ζεὺς νίκης καὶ δόξης ἐστὶ κύριος, καὶ τὸν
lines.en: that of Zeus Victory, since Zeus is lord of victory and glory, and that

lines.text: 15 Ἑρμοῦ Ἀνάγκην, ἐπειδὴ ὁ Ἑρμῆς κύριός ἐστι λόγου, ὁ δὲ λόγος
lines.en: 15 of Hermes Necessity, since Hermes is lord of reason, and reason

lines.text: ἀναγκαστικὸς ὑπάρχει, καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν τοὺς κλήρους ὡσαύτως κατὰ
lines.en: is compelling, and the lots of the rest likewise according to

lines.text: τὴν ἰδιοτροπίαν ἑκάστου τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀστέρων· καὶ ταῦτα μὲν περὶ τούτου.
lines.en: the peculiar nature of each of the seven stars; and these things concerning this.

lines.text: (Fol. 12v). Ἐπεὶ δὲ ἐν τῇ προλαβούσῃ θεωρίᾳ τὴν μέθοδον τῆς τῶν
lines.en: (Fol. 12v). But since in the preceding theory we postponed the method of the

lines.text: κλήρων εὑρέσεως ἀνεβαλόμεθα, φέρε νῦν ἐπικαίρως ταύτην παραδῶ-
lines.en: finding of the lots, come now let us opportunely hand this down-

sections.text:
1 Heliodori, Hermiae filii, qui circa annum 500 florebat, commentarium in Pauli
Alexandrini Εἰσαγωγὴν in pluribus codicibus traditur, et hoc opus inlustris astro-
nomi dignum est in primis quod edatur (cf. Catal. Venet., p. 81, n. 1). Quem laborem
cum nunc suscipere nequeamus, interim huius commentarii frustula quaedam
publici iuris facere visum est, quibus Heliodorus veterum scriptorum auctoritatem
invocat.
2 De hac Hermetis de sortibus doctrina, cf. Paul. Alex., I, 2v, et Catal. Flor.,
p. 168, 20 ss, p. 160, 12 ss. In codice Vaticano 1056, saec. XIV, f. 244, exstat
excerptum Περὶ τῶν ἑπτὰ κλήρων τῶν ἐν τῷ Παναρέτῳ.
sections.en:
1 The commentary of Heliodorus, son of Hermias, who flourished around the year 500, on the Introduction of Paulus Alexandrinus is handed down in several codices, and this work of the illustrious astronomer is especially worthy of being published (cf. Catal. Venet., p. 81, n. 1). Since we cannot undertake this labor now, it seemed good in the meantime to make public certain fragments of this commentary, in which Heliodorus invokes the authority of ancient writers.
2 Concerning this doctrine of Hermes on lots, cf. Paul. Alex., I, 2v, and Catal. Flor., p. 168, 20 ff, p. 160, 12 ff. In the Vatican codex 1056, 14th century, f. 244, there exists an excerpt Concerning the seven lots in the Panaretos.

summary.headline: The Seven Lots of Hermes
summary.text: Heliodorus’ commentary on Paulus Alexandrinus explains Hermes Trismegistus’s doctrine of the seven lots in the Panaretos, linking the Sun, Moon, Zeus, Hermes, Aphrodite, Ares, and Kronos with Good Daimon, Good Fortune, Victory, Necessity, Eros, Daring, and Nemesis.
